previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), left ventricular thrombus, chronic kidney disease, diabetes, and prior AAA repair was admitted for shortness of breath, back pain, and altered mental status. He had a mild CHF exacerbation with elevated BNP and interstitial edema on chest X-ray, treated with IV Lasix and transitioned to daily oral diuresis. His back pain was musculoskeletal, not renal, confirmed by CT. Altered mental status and sleep disturbances were attributed to an unintentional overdose of imipramine (125 mg vs. prescribed 62.5 mg), prompting a psychiatry consult and initiation of a taper. Warfarin was increased to 5 mg daily due to subtherapeutic INR, and plans were made for outpatient follow-up with vascular surgery, psychiatry, and GI for repeat capsule endoscopy. He stabilized, mental status improved, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and close follow-up.
